fixes.title: Light frames are written with NO pointing at all - no RA/DEC/OBJCTRA/OBJECT card and NULL mount_ra/mount_dec - after a successful slew to explicit coordinates
fixes.summary: Confirmed and fixed the FITS half at its cause: nothing on the sequencer capture path ever read the mount. FitsWriteHeaderRich::from_frame_context sets ra/dec from FrameContext.target_ra_hours/target_dec_degrees, which are only populated by a Target group - so a run built on 'Slew to Target' with custom coordinates produced frames with no RA/DEC/OBJCTRA/OBJCTDEC card at all, and even the Target-group path wrote the target's NOMINAL coordinates (0h/0deg for an unedited 'New Target') rather than where the scope actually was. BridgeDeviceOps (bridge/src/sequencer_ops.rs) is the DeviceOps the live sequencer runs on (sequencer_api.rs::api_sequencer_start -> sequencer_ops::create_device_ops), and its save_fits is the writer for every sequenced frame. Added BridgeDeviceOps::read_mount_pointing(), which resolves the connected mount via DeviceManager::first_connected_device_id(DeviceType::Mount) and reads mount_get_coordinates (one driver read, not the full mount_get_status capability sweep - that would cost ~10 COM round trips per saved frame on ASCOM), then derives altitude locally from the site via the calculate_altitude/get_observer_location helpers already in this file so AIRMASS becomes computable for sequenced frames for the first time. Header assembly moved out of save_fits into a testable build_rich_header(image_data, frame_ctx, pointing): the mount's report now wins over the target's nominal coordinates (RA/DEC mean 'where the telescope was', the MaxIm DL / N.I.N.A. convention, and it is also the right plate-solve search hint), with the target coordinates kept as the fallback so a run with no readable mount is no worse off than before. OBJECT still comes from the target name. Also de-rotted the module's `as`-cast policy index, whose line numbers had already drifted ~80 lines and which my insertion would have pushed further out - it is now keyed by function name.
fixes.test: 3 tests in native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/sequencer_ops.rs mod pointing_tests: untargeted_frame_carries_the_mount_pointing (full FITS write + read-back via save_fits_file_rich/read_fits, asserts RA=17h in degrees, DEC=30, OBJCTRA='17 00 00.00', OBJCTDEC='+30 00 00.00', AIRMASS present, on a FrameContext with NO target - the exact repro), mount_pointing_wins_over_nominal_target_coordinates (target 0h/0deg is overridden by the mount's 17h/30deg while OBJECT stays 'New Target'), missing_mount_falls_back_to_target_coordinates (no-regression guard for the no-mount case). Run: cargo test --package skotiq_bridge --lib pointing_tests
fixes.caveats: Verified fail-without-fix by neutering the pointing branch in build_rich_header (let _ = pointing;) and re-running: untargeted_frame_carries_the_mount_pointing failed with 'RA card must be present' and mount_pointing_wins_over_nominal_target_coordinates failed with left: Some(0.0) right: Some(17.0). Restored the fix; all 3 pass, and the full bridge lib suite is green (428 passed, 0 failed). The third test (no-mount fallback) passes either way by design - it is a no-regression guard, not the proof. Two limits: (1) read_mount_pointing itself is device I/O and is not unit-tested (thin delegation, like the rest of this adapter); (2) this fixes the FITS half only. The DB half (captured_images.mount_ra/mount_dec still NULL) needs the shared change described below, and the same pointing gap exists in the two OTHER DeviceOps impls I do not own - bridge/src/unified_device_ops.rs (used by api_sequencer_resume_from_checkpoint and api_sequencer_set_simulation_mode(false)) and bridge/src/real_device_ops.rs - so a RESUMED run still writes frames with no pointing.
fixes.needs_shared_change: 1) bridge/src/unified_device_ops.rs::save_fits and bridge/src/real_device_ops.rs::save_fits duplicate the same from_frame_context + gain/offset/temp patch block and have the identical pointing gap. Best fix: make build_rich_header (now in sequencer_ops.rs) or an equivalent helper the single shared header assembler and give all three impls the same mount read. Until then, a run resumed from a checkpoint writes pointing-less frames. 2) The comment at bridge/src/api/imaging.rs (from_frame_context, `altitude: None`) says AIRMASS 'needs the site location and capture time threaded into FrameContext' - the sequencer path now supplies altitude from the DeviceOps side, so that note should be updated to say it is the non-sequencer callers that still lack it. 3) The durable fix is to add mount_ra_hours/mount_dec_degrees/mount_altitude_deg/pier_side to skotiq_sequencer::scheduling::FrameContext and populate them in build_frame_context_for_save (sequencer/src/instructions.rs), where the focuser/rotator/guider live-telemetry reads already happen - then every save_fits impl gets it for free AND the same values are available to the frame event for the DB.

fixes.title: Captured frames are written to the DB with NO gain, offset, sensor temperature, mount pointing, focuser position or target link - although the FITS file it just wrote has all of them
fixes.summary: Real, independently re-confirmed, but every file that has to change is outside my ownership (native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/executor/** and bridge/src/sequencer_ops.rs). Traced the whole chain: the truth lives in FrameContext, which reaches bridge/src/sequencer_ops.rs::save_fits and goes into the FITS header - and then is thrown away. The DB row is built from a DIFFERENT source: sequencer/src/instructions.rs::emit_grade_progress emits ProgressDetail::FrameAccepted/FrameRejected (sequencer/src/node/progress.rs) carrying only node_id, hfr, eccentricity, star_count and save_path/reject_path; bridge/src/api/sequencer.rs maps it to SequencerEvent::FrameAccepted (bridge/src/event.rs); and Dart's _registerSequenceFrame (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/event_operations.dart:595) then RECONSTRUCTS the capture settings by walking the sequence tree (resolveFrameAttribution). That is why gain/offset are the ExposureNode's per-node OVERRIDE (NULL when the node runs on profile defaults, while the FITS card says 100/10), and why sensor_temp/cooler_power/mount_*/pier_side/focuser_*/rotator_angle are absent entirely - I verified images_dao.dart::insertSequenceFrame (line ~657) has no parameter for any of them, so that code path can never write those columns no matter what the event carries. The two sources cannot help but diverge because there is only one that is real.
fixes.test: None written - no change was made. Writing a test in my owned files would have asserted nothing about the defect, which lives entirely in the event payload and the Dart DAO.
fixes.caveats: Do not fix this by adding more fields to resolveFrameAttribution: that is the second source of truth and is exactly what makes the FITS and the DB disagree. The fix is to carry the FrameContext the FITS writer used onto the frame event.
fixes.needs_shared_change: One change, four files plus the migration, so the FITS header and the DB row are stamped from the same struct: (a) sequencer/src/node/progress.rs - widen ProgressDetail::FrameAccepted/FrameRejected with the per-frame capture truth (gain, offset, sensor_temp_c, cooler_power, mount_ra_hours, mount_dec_degrees, mount_altitude_deg, mount_azimuth_deg, pier_side, focuser_position, focuser_temperature_c, rotator_angle_deg, exposure_secs, bin_x, bin_y, frame_type, target_id); (b) sequencer/src/instructions.rs - emit_grade_progress already runs immediately after build_frame_context_for_save, so pass that same FrameContext in and populate the new fields from it rather than from ExposureConfig; add mount pointing + pier side to build_frame_context_for_save alongside the existing focuser/rotator/guider live reads (see item 3 of the other finding); (c) bridge/src/event.rs + bridge/src/api/sequencer.rs - widen SequencerEvent::FrameAccepted/FrameRejected and the PD-> SequencerEvent mapping identically (FRB regen required); (d) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/images_dao.dart - insertSequenceFrame currently has NO parameters for sensorTemp, coolerPower, mountRa/mountDec/mountAltitude/mountAzimuth, pierSide, focuserPosition, focuserTemp or rotatorAngle; add them and put the columns in the INSERT list; (e) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/event_operations.dart::_registerSequenceFrame - read gain/offset/binning/frameType/exposure from the EVENT and use resolveFrameAttribution only for the things the event genuinely cannot know (target row id, integration budgets). Regression test to add on the Dart side: seed a FrameAccepted event whose gain/offset differ from the producing node's overrides and assert the captured_images row matches the EVENT, not the node. Separately, target_id stays NULL because an ad-hoc Target node has no row in `targets` (the Session Report files those frames as 'Untargeted'); either persist ad-hoc targets on run start or accept and document the NULL - that is a product decision, not a wiring bug.
